title: Sutton Hoo ship burial (Mound 1)
summary: In Mound 1 at Sutton Hoo in Suffolk, near the River Deben, a 27.3-metre clinker-built ship held the burial of a king or great warrior of East Anglia about 1,400 years ago, in the 7th century. No body was found. King Rædwald is the most likely candidate. The site was first excavated in 1939 and again in 1966–1971.

uncertainty.note: National Trust: 1,400 years ago, burials date to the 7th century AD; the PMC article says 7th century AD.
